plan.title: Agreed to tonight's step before 9 am: no kickoff re-asking it

context.text: Morning! 7 hours last night, Whoop says 68% recovery. Not bad!
Not bad at all, Alex. Same again tonight: in bed at 9:30, screens away. You in?

transcript.text: Love it. Quick one about last night: what helped you wind down and actually get to sleep on time?
Hey Alex! Ten minutes to wind-down time. Start getting set up now: phone on the charger across the room, lights low, so you're in bed by 9:30. Send me a quick pic once you're settled.

checks.reason: No guilt or urgency; it simply moves on to asking about last night.
Asks a question ('what helped you wind down...') when the regression case calls for a brief warm answer with nothing more asked.
Warm enough, though 'Love it.' is a little flat for big energy.
Names the step: phone on the charger, lights low, in bed by 9:30.
Four short sentences, slightly over three, with no question at the end.
What (in bed, phone away, lights low) and when (9:30) are clear; the setup is concrete.
No teaching offered, which fits a simple reminder for a known routine.
Warm, direct and not overfamiliar, with no emoji row.

conversation.reason: The 9:20 pm check-in goes out ahead of the 9:30 step after the morning 'Yep!', and nothing says they've already started.
No kickoff is sent at 9 am or later; the morning conversation covered the step.
The 9:30 time is not restated in ZOH's reply to 'Yep!'; it only reappears in the later check-in.
The reply to 'Yep!' is warm and does not restate the time, but it asks a new question, which the regression case rules out.

grade.summary: ZOH avoided the old failures: it didn't repeat the time in its reply to 'Yep!' and sent no kickoff later in the morning, and the 9:20 pm check-in names the step clearly. It missed the regression case's key point by asking a follow-up question after 'Yep!' when it should have simply answered warmly and stopped.
